record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: What general classes of distributions or geometric spaces admit efficient random-walk sampling algorithms beyond convex bodies and logconcave densities? In particular, can one give a sufficient condition, formulated using isoperimetry together with a local regularity property of the target density, that guarantees efficient sampling, and for which manifolds with nonnegative curvature can such an efficient sampling process be defined?

evidence.quote: Our next open problem is to understand classes of distributions that can be efficiently sampled by random walks.

Can one provide a sufficient condition that depends on isoperimetry and some local property of the density to be sampled? More concretely, for what manifolds with nonnegative curvature (for which isoperimetry is known) can an efficient sampling process be defined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, connected, complete Riemannian manifold equipped with its Riemannian volume measure, and let $\pi$ be a probability density on $M$ (with respect to the volume measure). A random-walk sampling algorithm for $\pi$ is a Markov chain on $M$ whose stationary distribution is $\pi$; it is called efficient if its mixing time to $\varepsilon$ total-variation distance from $\pi$ is bounded by a polynomial in the dimension $n=\dim M$, in $\log(1/\varepsilon)$, and in natural geometric parameters of $(M,\pi)$ (such as diameter, smoothness constants, and a Cheeger / isoperimetric constant).

Recall that the Cheeger isoperimetric constant of $\pi$ is
$$\psi(\pi)=\inf_{S}\frac{\pi^{+}(\partial S)}{\min\{\pi(S),1-\pi(S)\}},$$
where the infimum is over measurable $S\subset M$ and $\pi^{+}$ denotes the boundary measure induced by $\pi$. A density $\pi=e^{-V}$ is said to satisfy a local regularity property if, for example, $V$ is locally Lipschitz, locally smooth, or has bounded local oscillation at an appropriate scale.

Problem. 
(a) Identify general classes of probability distributions, defined on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ or on Riemannian manifolds and going strictly beyond uniform distributions on convex bodies and logconcave densities, that admit efficient random-walk sampling algorithms in the sense above. 

(b) Formulate and prove a sufficient condition for efficient sampling that combines (i) a quantitative isoperimetric assumption on $(M,\pi)$ (a lower bound on $\psi(\pi)$ or a related Poincaré/log-Sobolev inequality) with (ii) a local regularity property of the target density $\pi$, and which implies that some explicit Markov chain (e.g., a ball walk, a Metropolis-adjusted walk, or a geodesic/Langevin walk) mixes in polynomial time.

(c) Determine, within the framework of part (b), the class of complete Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci (or sectional) curvature on which an efficient sampling process for the uniform distribution, or for sufficiently regular densities, can be explicitly defined and analyzed.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made since the question was posed. Mangoubi–Smith (2016/2018) proved rapid mixing of geodesic walks on manifolds with positive sectional curvature; Goyal–Shetty (2019) extended sampling/optimization to convex sets in Riemannian manifolds of nonnegative curvature; Klartag (2017) generalized localization to manifolds with Ricci lower bounds; and Vempala–Wibisono (2019) and follow-ups showed isoperimetry alone (Poincaré/log-Sobolev) plus smoothness of the potential suffices for rapid mixing of Langevin-type algorithms. A fully general characterization of distributions admitting efficient random-walk sampling remains open, but substantial sufficient conditions combining isoperimetry with local regularity are now established.

status_evidence.title: Rapid Mixing of Geodesic Walks on Manifolds with Positive Curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Geodesic walk on manifolds with positive sectional curvature bounded above and below mixes rapidly, with bound independent of dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Efficient random-walk sampling on positively curved manifolds is established.

status_evidence.title: Sampling and Optimization on Convex Sets in Riemannian Manifolds of Non-Negative Curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Goyal and Shetty extend efficient sampling/optimization to convex sets in Riemannian manifolds of nonnegative curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Direct progress on the nonnegative-curvature manifold sampling subproblem.

status_evidence.title: Rapid Convergence of the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm: Isoperimetry Suffices
status_evidence.snippet: Vempala–Wibisono show isoperimetric inequalities (Poincaré/LSI) plus smoothness of the potential give rapid convergence of Langevin sampling beyond logconcavity.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions combining isoperimetry with local regularity have been proven.

status_evidence.title: Needle decompositions in Riemannian geometry (Klartag)
status_evidence.snippet: Localization technique generalized to Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below.
status_evidence.claim: Isoperimetric tools needed for sampling extend to curved settings.
